definition_zh: 鱼；鱼类；钓鱼；捕鱼
definition_en: an animal that lives and swims in water and breathes through gills; also, to try to catch fish
core_image: 水里游动、用鳃呼吸、被鱼钩拉出水面的动物
scene: 清晨的湖面很安静，爷爷坐在小船上，把鱼竿甩进水里等着鱼上钩。My grandfather caught a big fish in the quiet lake at dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 fish 是「鱼」（第 1 个义项：生活在水里、用鳃呼吸的动物）；句意为爷爷清晨在安静的湖里钓到了一条大鱼。

senses.title: A water animal with gills
senses.definition: an animal that lives in water, swims with fins, and breathes through gills
senses.definitionCN: 生活在水里、用鳍游动、靠鳃呼吸的动物
senses.example: The pond is full of golden fish.
senses.why: The core image is a creature shaped by water, so every sense of fish starts from the swimming body.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是被水塑形的动物，fish 的每个义项都从这具游动的身体出发。

senses.title: The flesh of fish as food
senses.definition: the flesh of a fish eaten as food
senses.definitionCN: 作为食物的鱼肉
senses.example: We had grilled fish for dinner.
senses.why: Once the animal is known, the food made from it naturally takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 动物本身被认识之后，用它做的食物自然沿用同一个名字。

senses.title: To try to catch fish
senses.definition: to try to catch fish with a rod, nets, or lines
senses.definitionCN: 用鱼竿、渔网或钓线设法捕鱼
senses.example: They fish in the river every weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 他们每个周末都在河里钓鱼。
senses.why: Because people went after the swimming creature, the activity of catching it took the animal's name as a verb.
senses.whyCN: 因为人们追逐这种会游的动物，捕捉它的活动就用动物名作动词来指称。

senses.title: To search by feeling
senses.titleCN: 摸索着找；拐弯抹角地探听
senses.definition: to search for something inside a bag or pocket by feeling around
senses.definitionCN: 在包里或口袋里靠手摸来找东西
senses.example: She fished in her bag for the keys.
senses.exampleCN: 她在包里摸索着找钥匙。
senses.why: Pulling a key out of a bag looks like pulling a fish out of water, so the fishing motion extended to groping for anything.
senses.whyCN: 从包里摸出钥匙像把鱼拉出水面，于是捕捞的动作扩展为摸找任何东西。

intro.en: Fish is one of the oldest words in English, reaching back to the common Germanic language.
intro.cn: fish 是英语里最古老的词之一，可以追溯到共同日耳曼语。

items.en: The common Germanic form fiskaz gave related words across the family, from German Fisch to Dutch vis.
items.cn: 共同日耳曼语形式 fiskaz 在日耳曼语族各语言中留下了同源词，如德语 Fisch、荷兰语 vis。

items.en: Old English recorded fisc for both the animal and its flesh, and fiscian as the verb to fish.
items.cn: 古英语用 fisc 记录动物与鱼肉，并用 fiscian 表示捕鱼这个动词。

items.en: Old Norse fisk was closely related and reinforced the same word in the north of England.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 fisk 与它关系密切，在英格兰北部强化了同一个词。

items.en: Middle English kept fish in daily use as fishing became central to coastal life and trade.
items.cn: 中古英语延续 fish 的日常用法，捕鱼当时已成为沿海生活与贸易的中心。

items.en: Modern English added senses for the flesh on the plate and for fishing as sport and industry.
items.cn: 现代英语又增加盘中的鱼肉义，以及钓鱼作为运动和产业的用法。

definition_zh: 合身；适合；安装；健康的；发作
definition_en: to be the right size or shape; to be suitable; healthy and strong; a sudden attack of illness or emotion
core_image: 把零件放进刚好形状吻合的凹槽里
scene: 试衣间里她拉上裤子的拉链，裤子不大不小正正好。The new coat fits her perfectly.
sceneCN: 这里 fit 是「合身；大小合适」（第 1 个义项：尺寸或形状刚好吻合）；句意为新外套她穿正合身。

senses.title: To be the right size or shape
senses.definition: to be the correct size or shape for someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 尺寸或形状对某人某物刚好合适
senses.example: These shoes fit me well.
senses.why: Two shapes that match exactly are the picture behind every fit sense.
senses.whyCN: 两个形状恰好吻合，是 fit 一切义项背后的画面。

senses.title: To be suitable for a purpose
senses.definition: to be right or suitable for a purpose or job
senses.definitionCN: 对某个目的或工作来说是恰当的
senses.example: She is fit for the job.
senses.why: What matches the slot in shape also matches it in function, so size became suitability.
senses.whyCN: 形状吻合的也恰能在功能上匹配，尺寸义于是引申为合适义。

senses.title: To put something into place
senses.definition: to put a part or device into the right place
senses.definitionCN: 把部件或装置安到正确的位置
senses.example: The workers fit new locks on the doors.
senses.why: Making a part match its slot means putting it in, so the matching motion became installation.
senses.whyCN: 让部件与槽位吻合就意味着把它放进去，匹配的动作于是变成安装。

senses.title: Healthy and strong
senses.definition: physically healthy and able to work or exercise hard
senses.definitionCN: 身体健康的、能胜任劳作或锻炼的
senses.example: He keeps fit by running every day.
senses.why: A body ready for hard work is a body made to the right shape, so suitability became physical health.
senses.whyCN: 随时能干重活的身体就是被塑造成合适形状的身体，合适义由此落到健康上。

senses.title: A sudden attack of illness or emotion
senses.definition: a sudden short period of illness or of strong feeling
senses.definitionCN: 疾病或强烈情绪的突然短时爆发
senses.example: She had a fit of laughter.
senses.why: A seizure strikes suddenly like a part snapping into an unwanted place, so fit named sharp bursts.
senses.whyCN: 疾病发作像零件突然卡进不想要的位置，fit 于是被用来指急剧的爆发。

intro.en: Fit is an English word whose earliest sense was about matching and coming together.
intro.cn: fit 是一个英语本族词，最早的含义与吻合、凑合在一起有关。

items.en: Middle English had a verb fitten meaning to lead or adjust, and the noun fitte meaning a part of a poem.
items.cn: 中古英语有动词 fitten 意为引导、调整，名词 fitte 指诗歌的一个段落。

items.en: It is generally linked to a Germanic root meaning to tie or to join, the picture of parts coming together.
items.cn: 一般认为它出自日耳曼语词根，意为系、结，正是各部分合到一起的画面。

items.en: By the fifteenth century fitte also named a sudden outburst, from a fit of a song or laughter.
items.cn: 到十五世纪，fitte 也指突然的爆发，从歌曲或大笑的一阵引出。

items.en: Early Modern English fixed the senses of correct size, suitability and installation.
items.cn: 近代英语确立了尺寸合适、适用与安装等义项。

items.en: The health sense grew in the nineteenth century from exercise culture.
items.cn: 健康义项在十九世纪随锻炼文化兴起而生长。

note.en: Watch out for words next to fit that differ by one letter or one meaning.
note.cn: 留意与 fit 只差一个字母或一层含义的词。

senses.title: To repair something broken
senses.definition: to repair something that is broken or not working
senses.definitionCN: 把损坏或失灵的东西修好
senses.example: He fixed the broken chair.
senses.why: The core image is pressing a loose part back until it holds, and repair is the everyday result.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是把松脱的部件按压回原位使它稳固，修理是这一动作的日常结果。

senses.title: To fasten something firmly
senses.definition: to make something stay firmly in one place
senses.definitionCN: 使某物牢牢停留在某处
senses.example: They fixed the sign to the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把招牌固定在墙上。
senses.why: Before repairing comes holding still, so fix first meant making something unmoving.
senses.whyCN: 修理之前先要稳住，fix 最初就指使东西不动。

senses.title: To arrange or decide
senses.definition: to arrange or decide something in advance
senses.definitionCN: 事先安排或决定某事
senses.example: We fixed a date for the meeting.
senses.why: Fixing a date means making it unmovable, just like a nailed plank.
senses.whyCN: 定日期就是让它不可挪动，如同钉牢的木板。

senses.title: To prepare food or a drink
senses.definition: to make a meal or drink ready
senses.definitionCN: 把饭食或饮品准备好
senses.example: Mom fixed breakfast for us.
senses.exampleCN: 妈妈给我们准备了早餐。
senses.why: Preparing a meal is arranging things into their right places, an extension of making firm.
senses.whyCN: 备餐就是把各物安置到位，是「使稳固」义的延伸。

senses.title: A difficult situation
senses.definition: a difficult or awkward situation
senses.definitionCN: 困难或尴尬的局面
senses.example: We are in a real fix now.
senses.why: Being stuck like a fastened object turned into the picture of being trapped.
senses.whyCN: 像被钉住的东西一样动弹不得，转成了被困住的局面。

intro.en: Fix came from Latin through French, always about making things firm.
intro.cn: fix 经法语来自拉丁语，始终与「使牢固」有关。

items.en: Latin figere meant to fasten or drive in, the image of a nail going into wood.
items.cn: 拉丁语 figere 意为钉牢、钉入，是钉子打进木头的画面。

items.en: Medieval Latin fixare, a frequentative form, meant to make fast again and again.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 fixare 是反复动词形式，意为反复固定。

items.en: Old French fixer and the adjective fix carried the idea of firmness into French.
items.cn: 古法语 fixer 与形容词 fix 把牢固的观念带入法语。

items.en: English took fix in the fifteenth century mainly as an adjective and the sense of fastening.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪吸收 fix，主要作形容词及「固定」义。

items.en: By the nineteenth century fix was the everyday verb for repair, arrange and prepare in America.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，fix 在美国成为表示修理、安排、准备的日常动词。

note.cn: 下列与 fix 相邻的词值得清楚区分。

abstract.en: See a nail driven in, never moving again.
abstract.cn: 想象钉子被敲进木头再不动弹。

definition_en: a piece of cloth with a special design used as a symbol or signal; also, to mark something, or to become weak
core_image: 旗杆顶上迎风展开、招摇示意的一块布
scene: 运动场上，风把那块印着星星条纹的布吹得猎猎作响，全体起立注视。The national flag rose slowly up the pole.

senses.title: A cloth symbol or signal
senses.definition: a piece of cloth with a special design, used as a national symbol or a signal
senses.definitionCN: 带有特殊图案、用作国家象征或信号的布块
senses.example: Every country has its own flag.
senses.exampleCN: 每个国家都有自己的国旗。
senses.why: The core image is a cloth raised high so people far away can read its message.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是把布举到高处，让远处的人读懂它传递的信息。

senses.title: A marker used to show a place
senses.definition: a small marker, often on a map or in the ground, showing a spot
senses.definitionCN: 常出现在地图或地面上、用来标出位置的小标记
senses.example: The map puts a flag on the school.
senses.why: A flag marks a spot just as a national flag signals a country, so the sign spread to small markers.
senses.whyCN: 旗 signaling 国家，小旗 signaling 位置，标志义随之铺开。

senses.title: To mark something for attention
senses.definition: to mark a thing or a problem so people notice it
senses.definitionCN: 标记某物或某问题以引起注意
senses.example: Teachers flagged the errors in red.
senses.why: Raising a flag draws every eye, so to flag became to draw attention.
senses.whyCN: 升旗会吸引所有目光，flag 于是变成「提醒注意」。

senses.title: To become weak or tired
senses.definition: to become less strong, active, or eager
senses.definitionCN: 变得不如从前有力、活跃或热切
senses.example: His interest in chess flagged.
senses.exampleCN: 他对国际象棋的兴趣减退了。
senses.why: A loose flag hangs limp in no wind; the drooping cloth gave English this sense of fading strength.
senses.whyCN: 无风时旗布软垂，这幅下坠的画面给了英语「力量衰退」的含义。

intro.en: Flag has two old streams in English: one for the waving cloth, one for drooping weakness.
intro.cn: flag 在英语中有两条古老源流：一条指向飘扬的旗，一条指向低垂的疲软。

items.en: The cloth sense is usually linked to Old Norse flaka, meaning to hang loose like cloth.
items.cn: 布块义一般追溯到古诺斯语 flaka，意为像布那样松松垂挂。

items.en: Middle English flagge named a fluttering cloth, later a banner in the wind.
items.cn: 中古英语 flagge 指飘动的布，后来指风中招展的旗帜。

items.en: The weakness sense came from Old English flacca and other Germanic words meaning to droop.
items.cn: 疲软义来自古英语 flacca 及其他意为下垂的日耳曼词。

items.en: Both streams may share a Germanic root about things that flap or flop loosely.
items.cn: 两条源流可能共用一个表示松软摆动的日耳曼词根。

items.en: Modern English split the senses clearly: flags as symbols and markers, flagging as fading energy.
items.cn: 现代英语把各义分得很清楚：旗与标记属名词，疲软属动词。

note.en: Flag has sound-alikes and close neighbours worth checking.
note.cn: flag 有音近词与近邻词，值得核对。

definition_zh: 闪光；闪现；闪光灯；一瞬间
definition_en: a sudden bright light or a quick burst of light; to shine suddenly for a moment; to come or happen very quickly
core_image: 黑暗中骤然亮起又立刻熄灭的一道光
scene: 雷雨夜里，窗外忽然亮起一道白光，紧接着才传来雷声。A sudden flash of lightning lit up the sky.
sceneCN: 这里 flash 是名词「闪光；闪现」（第 1 个义项：突然亮起又很快消失的光）；句意为骤然一道闪电照亮天空。

senses.title: A sudden burst of light
senses.definition: a sudden bright light that lasts only a moment
senses.definitionCN: 只持续一瞬的强烈亮光
senses.example: A flash of lightning lit the field.
senses.why: The core image is light that appears and dies within a blink.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是眨眼之间亮起又熄灭的光。

senses.title: The device that produces light
senses.definition: the lamp on a camera that produces a sudden bright light
senses.definitionCN: 相机上发出骤然强光的装置
senses.example: Turn off the camera flash in the museum.
senses.exampleCN: 在博物馆里请关掉相机闪光灯。
senses.why: The light itself was named first, then the tool that makes it.
senses.whyCN: 先有光的名字，后有制造这种光的器具。

senses.title: A very short moment
senses.definition: a very short period of time
senses.definitionCN: 极短的片刻
senses.example: The answer came in a flash.
senses.why: Light lasts a blink, so the word measured time as brief as the light.
senses.whyCN: 光只存在一眨眼，这个词于是也用来度量同样短暂的时间。

senses.title: To shine or appear suddenly
senses.definition: to shine suddenly and briefly, or to appear in the mind suddenly
senses.definitionCN: 骤然亮起片刻，或在脑海中突然浮现
senses.example: Her name flashed across the screen.
senses.exampleCN: 她的名字在屏幕上一闪而过。
senses.why: What flashes in the eye also flashes in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 在眼前闪过的，也在心里闪现。

senses.title: To move very fast
senses.definition: to move past very quickly
senses.definitionCN: 极快地掠过
senses.example: A red car flashed by on the road.
senses.exampleCN: 一辆红车在公路上飞驰而过。
senses.why: Speed so great it blurs looks like light jumping from place to place.
senses.whyCN: 快到模糊的速度，看上去就像光从一个点跳到另一个点。

senses.title: The Act of Flying
senses.definition: the action or process of moving through the air on wings or in an aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 凭借翅膀或飞行器在空中移动的动作或过程
senses.example: The gulls' flight over the harbour lasted only a few seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 海鸥掠过港湾的飞行只持续了几秒钟。
senses.why: flyht is the bare action noun built on the verb fleogan 'to fly'; the suffix -t turns the doing into a thing you can name.
senses.whyCN: flyht 是由动词 fleogan「飞」直接构成的动作名词，后缀 -t 把「做」变成可以命名的「事」。

senses.title: A Scheduled Air Journey
senses.definition: a trip made by air, especially one operated on a regular service between two places
senses.definitionCN: 乘飞机的一次行程，尤指两地间按班期运营的航次
senses.example: Our flight to Denver leaves before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 我们飞往丹佛的航班在黎明前起飞。
senses.why: a scheduled service is one completed act of flying, so the uncountable action is counted out into separate items.
senses.whyCN: 一次班期服务就是一整次完成的飞行，于是不可数的动作被切分成一个个可数的班次。

senses.title: A Flock on the Wing
senses.definition: a group of birds or aircraft moving through the air together
senses.definitionCN: 一起在空中移动的一群鸟或飞行器
senses.example: A flight of geese crossed the marsh at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 一群大雁在黄昏时飞越沼泽。
senses.why: the collective noun applies the action to the whole body that performs it at one time, so the group is named after its flight.
senses.whyCN: 这个集合名词把动作归给同时做出它的整个群体，于是这一群就以「飞行」命名。

senses.title: A Set of Stairs
senses.definition: a continuous run of steps between one floor or landing and the next
senses.definitionCN: 两层楼或两个平台之间连续的一串台阶
senses.example: She carried the box up the last flight of stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 她把箱子搬上了最后一段楼梯。
senses.why: a run of steps rises step after step like a body climbing through air, so English lent the word for flying to this rising series.
senses.whyCN: 一串台阶一级接一级地上升，像身体在空中爬升，英语于是把「飞行」这个词借给了这道上升的序列。

senses.title: Escape by Running
senses.definition: the act of fleeing or being driven away from danger
senses.definitionCN: 逃离危险或被赶离现场的行为
senses.example: The intruders were put to flight by a single shout.
senses.exampleCN: 一声喊叫就把闯入者赶跑了。
senses.why: fleeing is the oldest figurative use of flying: the body takes off as if on wings, so the same noun covers panic movement on the ground.
senses.whyCN: 逃跑是「飞」最古老的比喻用法：身体仿佛长了翅膀般离开，同一个名词因此也指地面上的仓皇移动。

senses.title: Path of a Projectile
senses.definition: the curved course followed by an arrow, bullet or ball through the air
senses.definitionCN: 箭、子弹或球在空中划出的弧线路径
senses.example: The arrow's flight flattened as it lost speed.
senses.exampleCN: 箭在速度衰减时，飞行弧线变得平缓。
senses.why: a projectile repeats the core action without wings: it too crosses the air along a line, and the line is named after the crossing.
senses.whyCN: 抛射体没有翅膀却重复了核心动作：它也沿一条线穿过空气，这条线就以「穿越」命名。

senses.title: Flight of Fancy
senses.definition: a burst of imaginative invention that has little grounding in fact
senses.definitionCN: 一段缺少事实依据的想象性发挥
senses.example: The plan was a flight of fancy that no budget could support.
senses.exampleCN: 那项计划纯属异想天开，没有哪份预算支撑得起。
senses.why: the mind is pictured as taking off and leaving the ground of fact, exactly the movement the word already names.
senses.whyCN: 这里把心智想象成起飞、离开事实的地面，正是这个词本已命名的那个动作。

senses.title: Feathers on an Arrow
senses.definition: the feathers fitted near the head of an arrow shaft to keep it steady in flight
senses.definitionCN: 装在箭杆尾端附近、使箭飞行稳定的羽毛
senses.example: He replaced the torn flight on the arrow before the match.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛前他换掉了箭上破损的箭羽。
senses.why: the feather is the part that makes the arrow fly straight, so the effect is named by the very act it serves.
senses.whyCN: 羽毛正是让箭飞得笔直的那一部分，于是这一部件用它服务的那个动作来命名。

intro.en: Flight comes straight from Old English flyht, an action noun made from the strong verb fleogan 'to fly' plus the suffix -t. The family is Germanic, not Latin.
intro.cn: flight 直接来自古英语 flyht，是由强动词 fleogan「飞」加后缀 -t 构成的动作名词；整个词族属日耳曼语，与拉丁语无关。

items.en: Fleogan was the everyday verb 'to fly', a strong verb of the second class, and it is the direct ancestor of modern fly.
items.cn: fleogan 是日常表示「飞」的动词，属第二类强动词，是现代 fly 的直接祖先。

items.en: Old English formed action nouns by adding -t to a verb stem, as in gift from giefan and weight from wegan; flyht follows the same pattern.
items.cn: 古英语在动词词干后加 -t 构成动作名词，如 gift 来自 giefan、weight 来自 wegan；flyht 遵循同一模式。

items.en: Flyht meant both the act of flying and a flying group, and it already carried the sense of fleeing from an enemy.
items.cn: flyht 既指飞行的动作，也指飞行的群体，并且已经带有「逃避敌人」的意思。

items.en: Middle English flight kept the noun while the verb became fly; the staircase sense appears in the record later, formed on the image of a rising run of steps.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了名词 flight，动词则演变为 fly；楼梯义在文献中出现较晚，建立在「一级级上升」的意象上。

items.en: German Flug 'flight' and Dutch vlucht are built from the same verb with the same suffix, which confirms the pattern rather than any Latin source.
items.cn: 德语 Flug「飞行」与荷兰语 vlucht 由同一动词加同一后缀构成，这证实了该构词模式，而非任何拉丁来源。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Germanic only): the deeper Indo-European root behind fleogan is a reconstruction, and the arrow-feather sense has no firm first date.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅限日耳曼语之前）：fleogan 背后更早的印欧词根属重构形式，箭羽义的可靠首见年代亦不可考。

note.en: Group one holds words that resemble flight in spelling or sound but mostly belong to other roots; group two holds the travel and airborne words that overlap with one or another of its senses.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写或读音近似、但多数属于其他词根的词；第二组是在某个义项上与 flight 重叠的旅行与空中词汇。

entries.definition: Sudden fear; from Old English fyrhto, a noun of fear, with no connection to flying and no shared root with flight.
entries.definitionCN: 指突如其来的恐惧；来自古英语 fyrhto「恐惧」，与飞行无关，也与 flight 不同词根。

entries.definition: A group of ships, from Old English flēot, tied to flēotan 'to float'; the adjective fleet 'fast' is a separate Norse borrowing, so neither is kin to flight.
entries.definitionCN: 指船队，来自古英语 flēot，与 flēotan「漂浮」相关；形容词 fleet「快速」另从古诺斯语借入，二者都不是 flight 的同源词。

entries.definition: Built on flight plus -y, originally 'given to flight', hence fickle or frivolous; it shares the root but describes temperament.
entries.definitionCN: 由 flight 加 -y 构成，本义为「爱飞的」，引申为轻浮善变；词根相同，但描述的是性情。

entries.definition: To grow feathers fit for flight, from Old English -flycge 'fit to fly'; it belongs to the same flying family, though the exact link to fleogan is not settled.
entries.definitionCN: 指长出适合飞行的羽毛，来自古英语 -flycge「适合飞的」；属于同一「飞」词族，但它与 fleogan 的确切关系尚无定论。

entries.definition: A travel from one place to another by any means; flight is one kind of journey, limited to the air and to a single scheduled leg.
entries.definitionCN: 指以任何方式从一地到另一地的旅行；flight 是其中一种，限于空中且指单个航段。

entries.definition: A long journey, especially by sea or into space; it stresses distance and endurance rather than the act of flying.
entries.definitionCN: 指长途旅行，尤指海上或太空航行；强调距离与耐力，而非飞行动作。

entries.definition: To fly without flapping, riding rising air; it names one style of flight rather than flight as a category.
entries.definitionCN: 指不扇翅、借上升气流滑翔高飞；它命名的是飞行的一种方式，而非飞行这个类别。

entries.definition: The act of getting free from confinement or danger; it overlaps with flight in the sense of fleeing but says nothing about wings.
entries.definitionCN: 指摆脱拘禁或危险；在「逃跑」义上与 flight 重叠，但不含翅膀的意象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real cognates and real idioms, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的同源词与真实习语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: fleogan 'to fly' + -t: the act noun is built straight from the verb, exactly as gift is built on give.
normal.cn: fleogan「飞」+ -t：动作名词直接从动词构成，正如 gift 由 give 构成。

normal.en: German Flug and Dutch vlucht repeat the same verb-plus-suffix pattern, which fixes the shape of the word.
normal.cn: 德语 Flug 与荷兰语 vlucht 重复了同一套「动词加后缀」的模式，固定了这个词的形状。

normal.en: The staircase sense keeps the shape of the core image: a series climbing, step after step.
normal.cn: 楼梯义保留了核心意象的形状：一级接一级地向上攀升。

normal.en: put to flight means to make someone fly away, and take flight means to leave the ground or to run.
normal.cn: put to flight 意为使人飞逃，take flight 意为离地起飞或逃走。

normal.en: The family runs fly, flight, flighty, flightless, flighted.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 fly、flight、flighty、flightless、flighted。

abstract.en: Picture a spiral staircase seen from above: each step is one beat of a wing.
abstract.cn: 想象从上方俯瞰一道螺旋楼梯：每一级台阶就是一次振翅。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow's feather slicing the air, correcting the shaft with every wobble.
abstract.cn: 想象箭尾的羽毛切开空气，每一次晃动都被它矫正。

abstract.en: Picture a line of geese at dusk, one continuous stroke drawn across the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象黄昏时一列大雁，在天幕上画出一道连续的笔画。

examples.en: The engineer traced the flight of the ball with a slow-motion camera.
examples.cn: 工程师用慢动作摄影机追踪球的飞行轨迹。

examples.en: Bad weather forced the airline to cancel every flight before noon.
examples.cn: 恶劣天气迫使航空公司在中午前取消了所有航班。

examples.en: A flight of swallows passed low over the harvested field.
examples.cn: 一群燕子低低掠过收割后的田野。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「弗莱特」——像滑过天空的一道亮线，一掠而过 → 飞行；再想那段楼梯，也是一级级往上「飞」。

root: 古英语 flyht「飞行、飞行的群体」，由 fleogan「飞」（现代 fly 的祖先）+ 动作名词后缀 -t 构成，日耳曼语族，与德语 Flug、荷兰语 vlucht 同型；fleogan 更早的印欧词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses hang on one movement: something leaves the ground and travels a line through air. Counting that movement gives a flight number, grouping it gives a flock, copying it on the ground gives stairs, fleeing gives escape, and the line it draws gives the trajectory and the feather that steadies it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都挂在同一个动作上：某物离地，在空中走出一条线。把这一动作计数，就有航班号；把做出它的群体归拢，就有鸟群；让它在土地上复制，就有楼梯；用它来逃离，就有逃跑；把那条线取下来，就有弹道，也有让箭沿线的箭羽。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body leaving the ground and drawing a line through the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个身体离地，在空中划出一道线。

branches.en: THE ACTION ITSELF: flying, then one finished act of it counted as a scheduled trip.
branches.cn: 动作本身：先有飞行，再把一次完成的飞行计作一个班次。

branches.en: WHAT CARRIES THE MOTION: the flock that flies and the feather that keeps the arrow flying true.
branches.cn: 承载动作之物：飞行的鸟群，以及让箭飞直的羽毛。

branches.en: RISING IN PLACE: a run of steps repeats the climb without any air.
branches.cn: 原地上升：一串台阶在没有空气的地方重复了攀爬。

branches.en: FLYING AWAY: panic turns the same noun into escape.
branches.cn: 飞离：惊慌把同一个名词变成逃跑。

branches.en: THE DRAWN LINE: a projectile follows it literally, a daydream follows it in the mind.
branches.cn: 画出的线：抛射体在实处沿着它，白日梦在心上沿着它。

intro.en: Flight reads as two pieces: the Germanic verb stem for flying, and an old action-noun suffix. Everything else in the family is built by adding English endings to this noun.
intro.cn: flight 可以拆成两段：表「飞」的日耳曼动词词干，以及一个古老的动作名词后缀；词族中其余的词都是在这个名词上再加英语词尾构成的。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin entry to give: flight is Germanic throughout, and its cognates are German Flug and Dutch vlucht, not any Latin noun.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词形可列：flight 全程属日耳曼语，同源词是德语 Flug 与荷兰语 vlucht，而非任何拉丁名词。

items.structure: fleogan (Old English strong verb, class II)
items.meaning: to move through the air on wings
items.example: The stem supplies the bare act of flying.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干提供「飞」这一纯粹的动作。

items.structure: -t (Old English action-noun suffix, as in gift, weight)
items.meaning: the act or result of doing the verb
items.meaningCN: 动词所指动作或其结果
items.example: Add -t to the verb and the flying becomes a thing.
items.exampleCN: 在动词后加 -t，飞行就变成一件可以指称的事。

items.meaning: the act of flying; a flying group; a fleeing
items.example: Flight is recorded in Old English as flyht.
items.exampleCN: flight 在古英语中写作 flyht。

items.meaningCN: 爱飞的，引申为轻浮善变的
items.example: A flighty person is one whose attention keeps taking off.
items.exampleCN: flighty 的人，注意力总在起飞。

items.example: A flighted arrow carries its own stabiliser.
items.exampleCN: 装有箭羽的箭自带稳定器。

items.example: The suffix removes exactly the capacity the noun names.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀恰好去掉了名词所指的那种能力。

items.meaning: the route or line along which something flies
items.example: Controllers cleared the aircraft along a new flight path.
items.exampleCN: 管制员让这架飞机沿一条新飞行路线通行。

items.meaning: the cockpit, or the deck where aircraft take off
items.example: The flight deck is the part of the ship given to flying.
items.exampleCN: 飞行甲板是舰上专门交给飞行使用的那部分。

items.example: The missile was destroyed in flight.
items.exampleCN: 导弹在飞行途中被摧毁。

definition_zh: 地板；地面；楼层；海底；使困惑
definition_en: the surface you stand on inside a room; a level of a building; the ground or seabed
core_image: 房间底下承住双脚的那块平面
scene: 阳光从窗户照进来，落在擦得发亮的木板平面上。The cat sleeps on the warm wooden floor.
sceneCN: 这里 floor 是「地板」（第 1 个义项：房间里供人踩踏的平面）；句意为猫睡在温暖的木地板上。

derivatives.zh: 由 floor 加动名词后缀构成，义为「铺地材料；铺地板工程」
由 floor 加 board 构成，义为「地板条」

senses.title: The surface you stand on
senses.definition: the flat surface inside a room that people walk on
senses.definitionCN: 房间内供人行走的平坦表面
senses.example: The kitchen floor is tiled.
senses.why: The core image is the flat plane holding up your feet.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是承住双脚的平坦面。

senses.title: A level of a building
senses.definition: one of the levels of a building
senses.definitionCN: 建筑物的一个层级
senses.example: Our classroom is on the third floor.
senses.why: A building is floors stacked on floors, so each level took the name of its surface.
senses.whyCN: 楼房由一层层平面叠起，每个层级便以那个平面命名。

senses.title: The ground or seabed
senses.definition: the bottom surface of the sea, a cave, or a forest
senses.definitionCN: 海洋、洞穴或森林的底部
senses.example: Fish hide among rocks on the ocean floor.
senses.exampleCN: 鱼在海底的岩石间躲藏。
senses.why: Whatever lies beneath living things is their floor, on land or under water.
senses.whyCN: 无论陆地还是水下，生物脚下之物就是它们的 floor。

senses.title: To shock someone so they cannot answer
senses.definition: to surprise someone so much that they cannot reply or act
senses.definitionCN: 让某人惊讶得无法回应
senses.example: The tricky question floored him.
senses.exampleCN: 那个刁钻问题把他问倒了。
senses.why: Knocked flat on the floor cannot speak, so flooring someone means stopping them cold.
senses.whyCN: 被打倒在地板上的人说不出话，flooring 某人即让他当场语塞。

intro.en: Floor is an old English word for the level ground you tread.
intro.cn: floor 是一个古老的英语词，指踩踏的水平面。

items.en: Old English had flor, meaning the ground of a room or a beaten earth surface.
items.cn: 古英语作 flor，指房间的地面或夯实的土地面。

items.en: Old Norse flor was closely related and helped keep the word alive in the north.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 flor 与之关系密切，帮助这个词在北方存续。

items.en: It traces to a Germanic root about a flat, spread-out plane, related to flaw and lay.
items.cn: 它可追溯到一个表示平坦铺开的日耳曼词根，与 flaw、lay 相关。

items.en: Middle English extended floor from room ground to building levels.
items.cn: 中古英语把 floor 从房间地面扩展到建筑层级。

items.en: Modern English added the seabed sense and the stunned sense of being floored.
items.cn: 现代英语又增加了海底义与「被问倒」的引申义。

note.en: Floor and its neighbours are easy to mix; check each use.
note.cn: floor 与其近邻容易混淆，用法要逐一核对。

normalIntro.en: Five anchors for the word floor.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚定 floor 记忆的方法。

normal.en: floor rhymes with more and door.
normal.cn: floor 与 more、door 押韵。

normal.en: flour is flour, floor is floor; both sound alike in British English.
normal.cn: flour 是面粉，floor 是地板，英音读音相同。

normal.en: the ground floor is the level at street level.
normal.cn: ground floor 指临街的一层。

normal.en: the ocean floor is the bottom of the sea.
normal.cn: ocean floor 指海底。

normal.en: be floored means be so surprised you cannot speak.
normal.cn: be floored 表示惊讶得说不出话。

abstract.en: Feel the cool flat boards under your bare feet.
abstract.cn: 想象赤脚踩在凉爽平坦的木板上。

abstract.en: See a lift panel with buttons from one to ten.
abstract.cn: 想象电梯按钮从一层排到十层。

abstract.en: See sunlight lying in a bright square on the boards.
abstract.cn: 想象阳光在地板上铺出亮方格。

examples.en: Do not leave toys on the floor.
examples.cn: 不要把玩具丢在地板上。

senses.definitionCN: 把柔软之物弯折，使一部分盖住另一部分
senses.example: He folded the map along the crease.
senses.exampleCN: 他沿折痕把地图折起来。
senses.why: The core image is one flat layer lying down onto another.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一层平面倒伏叠上另一层。

senses.title: To bring arms or hands together
senses.definition: to bring the arms, hands or wings closely together
senses.definitionCN: 把双臂、双手或翅膀合到一起
senses.example: She folded her hands on the desk.
senses.why: Flat limbs lay one over another exactly like folded paper.
senses.whyCN: 扁平的手臂相互叠放，与折纸的动作如出一辙。

senses.title: A line where something is folded
senses.definition: a line or crease made by folding
senses.definitionCN: 折叠后留下的线条
senses.example: Iron out the folds in the shirt.
senses.why: The act leaves its mark, and the mark got the verb's name.
senses.whyCN: 动作留下痕迹，痕迹便以动词命名。

senses.title: A pen for sheep
senses.definition: an enclosure for sheep on a farm
senses.definitionCN: 农场里圈羊的围栏
senses.example: The sheep returned to the fold at dusk.
senses.why: A fence closes in on itself like a folded wall around the flock.
senses.whyCN: 围栏像一道折拢的墙，把羊群圈在其中。

senses.title: To close a business
senses.definition: to close because of failure, as a company does
senses.definitionCN: 公司因经营失败而关门
senses.example: The bakery folded after two years.
senses.exampleCN: 那家面包店两年后倒闭了。
senses.why: A business folding up closes like folded paper, pressed flat and finished.
senses.whyCN: 企业收摊如同纸被折平压扁，就此了结。

intro.en: Fold comes from an old English verb about doubling things over.
intro.cn: fold 来自古英语中表示把东西叠起的动词。

items.en: Old English had faldan or fealdan, to fold or double over.
items.cn: 古英语作 faldan 或 fealdan，意为折叠、对折。

items.en: It traces to common Germanic falthan, shared with German falten and Dutch vouwen.
items.cn: 它可追溯到共同日耳曼语 falthan，与德语 falten、荷兰语 vouwen 同源。

items.en: Old English also had falod for the sheep pen, a related but separate word.
items.cn: 古英语另有 falod 指羊栏，是相关但独立的词。

items.en: Middle English merged the spellings into fold for both senses.
items.cn: 中古英语把两个含义的拼写合并为 fold。

items.en: Modern English added the business sense of folding up, like paper pressed shut.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了企业收摊的比喻义，如纸被折平。

definition_zh: 跟随；接着；遵循；听懂；关注
definition_en: to go or come after someone or something; to act according to; to understand; to watch with interest
core_image: 沿着前面那人的脚印一直走下去
scene: 林间小路上，孩子们一个牵着一个排成一列往前走。Follow me and do not look back.
sceneCN: 这里 follow 是动词「跟随」（第 1 个义项：走在某人后面、循其路线）；句意为跟着我，不要回头看。

derivatives.zh: 由 follow 加名词后缀构成，义为「追随者；粉丝」

senses.title: To go after someone
senses.definition: to go or come after a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 走在一个或物之后
senses.example: The dog follows its owner everywhere.
senses.why: The core image is walking on the same track behind another.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是沿同一轨迹走在他人身后。

senses.title: To act according to rules or advice
senses.definition: to obey rules, or to act as advised
senses.definitionCN: 按规则行事或照建议行动
senses.example: Drivers must follow the traffic rules.
senses.exampleCN: 司机必须遵守交通规则。
senses.why: Rules walk ahead of us like guides, so obeying them is following.
senses.whyCN: 规则像向导走在前面，服从它们就是跟随。

senses.title: To happen after in time
senses.definition: to happen after something else in time or order
senses.definitionCN: 在时间或顺序上接在别的事之后
senses.example: Dinner followed the meeting.
senses.why: One event walking behind another in time mirrors people on a path.
senses.whyCN: 时间上一前一后的事件，正如路上前后而行的人。

senses.title: To understand what is said
senses.definition: to understand spoken words or a story
senses.definitionCN: 听明白话语或故事
senses.example: Do you follow what I mean?
senses.why: Keeping pace with an argument is keeping pace with a speaker.
senses.whyCN: 跟上论证的节奏，就是跟上说话人的脚步。

senses.title: To watch with interest
senses.definition: to pay close attention to news, sport, or social media accounts
senses.definitionCN: 密切留意新闻、体育或社交账号
senses.example: Millions follow this star online.
senses.exampleCN: 数百万人网上关注这位明星。
senses.why: Eyes, like feet, can trail a person day after day.
senses.whyCN: 目光如脚步，可以日复一日追着一个人。

items.en: Modern media added watching news and social accounts, the newest sense.
items.cn: 现代媒体增添了关注新闻与社交账号这一最新义项。

sceneCN: 这里 food 是名词「食物」（第 1 个义项：供人食用以维持生命之物）；句意为学校食堂中午供应健康的饭菜。

senses.title: Things eaten to live and grow
senses.definition: anything that people or animals eat for life and growth
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物为生存与生长而吃的东西
senses.example: Rice is the main food here.
senses.why: The core image is whatever enters the mouth to become strength.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一切入口后化为力气的东西。

senses.title: Nourishment for mind or plants
senses.definition: something that supports thought, feeling, or plant growth
senses.definitionCN: 支撑思想、情感或植物生长的养分
senses.example: Books are food for the mind.
senses.why: Whatever feeds the mind works like bread feeds the body.
senses.whyCN: 喂养头脑之物，如面包喂养身体。

senses.title: A particular kind of eaten things

senses.definitionCN: 某一类加工或天然食品

senses.why: The general meal-word counts its kinds one by one.

items.en: The plural foods appeared when kinds of food needed counting.

items.en: Modern English uses food for bodily meals, mind meals, and food chains in nature.
items.cn: 现代英语中 food 兼指身体之食、精神之食与自然界的食物链。

definition_en: the body part you stand and walk on; a unit of length; the lowest part of something; also, to walk or pay
core_image: 承住全身重量、带我们走路的脚掌
scene: 沙滩上留下两行深深的脚印，一直延伸到海浪边。He walked the whole way on foot.
sceneCN: 这里 foot 与 on 搭配表示「步行」（第 5 个义项：以脚代车出行）；句意为他全程步行。

senses.title: The body part you stand on
senses.definition: the lower limb of the body used for standing and walking
senses.definitionCN: 身体用来站立与行走的下肢末端
senses.example: My right foot hurts after the run.
senses.why: The core image is the base that carries the whole body.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是承载全身的基础。

senses.title: A unit of length
senses.definition: a measure of length equal to twelve inches
senses.definitionCN: 等于十二英寸的长度单位
senses.example: The room is fifteen feet wide.
senses.why: Measuring with real feet came first, then the unit fixed the name.
senses.whyCN: 先用真脚量地，单位沿用其名。

senses.title: The lowest part of something
senses.definition: the bottom or lowest end of a hill, page, or bed
senses.definitionCN: 山、页、床等的最低处
senses.example: We camped at the foot of the mountain.
senses.why: Whatever a body stands on is its foot, even for mountains.
senses.whyCN: 身体所立之处即其 foot，山亦如此。

senses.title: To pay a bill
senses.definition: to pay for something, especially a shared cost
senses.definitionCN: 为某物付款，尤指共同开销
senses.example: Dad footed the bill for dinner.
senses.why: Standing firm on a bill is like standing on your feet to settle it.
senses.whyCN: 稳稳立住账单，如用脚立定把账结清。

senses.title: To walk; going on foot
senses.definition: to walk, or travelling by walking
senses.definitionCN: 走路，或以走路方式出行
senses.example: They footed it across town.
senses.why: The organ names its own action, as wings give us to fly.
senses.whyCN: 器官之名转指其动作，如翅膀之于飞行。

items.en: Middle English kept foot for the unit of twelve inches in trade and building.
items.cn: 中古英语在商业与营造中以 foot 作十二英寸单位。

items.en: Modern English added idioms like foot the bill and on foot.
items.cn: 现代英语又添 foot the bill、on foot 等习语。

note.en: Foot carries irregular plural feet; mind it and its cousins.

senses.title: A push or pull that changes motion
senses.titleCN: 改变运动或形状的推拉力
senses.definition: a physical push or pull that can change the speed, direction or shape of a body
senses.definitionCN: 能改变物体速度、方向或形状的物理推拉作用
senses.example: The net force on the cart equals its mass times its acceleration.
senses.exampleCN: 小车所受的合力等于质量乘以加速度。
senses.why: Latin fortis meant strong, and mechanics took the word for the measurable quantity that makes a body move or bend.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 fortis 意为强壮，力学借这个词来指使物体运动或弯曲的可测之量。

senses.title: Strength of body or blow
senses.definition: muscular strength, or the power carried by a blow, a throw or a wave
senses.definitionCN: 肌肉的力量，或一击、一掷、一道浪所带的威力
senses.example: The force of the wave knocked the swimmer off her feet.
senses.exampleCN: 浪的力量把游泳者掀翻。
senses.why: Before physics existed, force was simply the strength that a body or a blow carries.
senses.whyCN: 在物理学出现之前，force 就是身体或一击所带的力气。

senses.title: Compulsion against resistance
senses.titleCN: 对抵抗施加的强制与武力
senses.definition: the use of pressure or violence to make someone do something against their will
senses.definitionCN: 用压力或暴力使人违背意愿地做某事
senses.example: The door yielded only to force.
senses.exampleCN: 那扇门只有靠强力才被打开。
senses.why: A strong hand can push a person as it pushes a door, so bodily strength became compulsion.
senses.whyCN: 强壮的手能推人，也能推门，于是体力这一义引申为强制。

senses.title: Binding power of law or rule
senses.definition: the legal or formal power that makes a rule, agreement or order binding
senses.definitionCN: 使规则、协议或命令具有约束力的法律或正式效力
senses.example: The new rules came into force at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定在午夜开始生效。
senses.why: A rule in force has the strength of an authority behind it, as if it could push a person into line.
senses.whyCN: 处于生效状态的规则背后有权威的力量，仿佛能把人推回队列。

senses.title: Power to convince
senses.definition: the strength of an argument, feeling or habit to move people's minds or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 论点、情感或习惯打动人心、改变行为的力量
senses.example: The force of her argument silenced the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她论证的力量让全场静了下来。
senses.why: An argument moves a mind the way a hand moves a body, so the same word covers mental pushing.
senses.whyCN: 论证推动人心，正如手推动身体，因此同一个词也指精神上的推力。

senses.title: An armed body of people
senses.definition: an organized body of soldiers, police or other armed personnel
senses.definitionCN: 有组织的军人、警察或其他武装人员群体
senses.example: The peacekeeping force reached the border at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 维和部队在黎明时抵达边境。
senses.why: Strength collected into a unit is spoken of as a force, a collective use of the same noun.
senses.whyCN: 把力量聚成一个单位，就说成一支 force，这是同一名词的集体用法。

senses.title: Manpower counted as a group
senses.definition: the number of people available for work, or a group treated as a single power
senses.definitionCN: 可供工作的人数，或被当作一股力量的人群
senses.example: The factory's labour force grew by a third in two years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂的劳动力两年间增加了三分之一。
senses.why: Once force meant strength in numbers, any body of workers could be counted as a force.
senses.whyCN: 当 force 指人数所聚的力量，任何一群工人也能被计为一股 force。

senses.title: To make something happen by pressure
senses.definition: to cause something to happen or to move by using pressure, effort or necessity
senses.definitionCN: 借助压力、努力或情势使某事发生或移动
senses.example: Illness forced him to give up the night shift.
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb: to put strength behind something until it yields.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：把力量压到某事背后，直到它让步。

intro.en: Force comes through Old French from late Latin fortia, a plural noun of strength built on fortis 'strong'. The physics sense dates from the seventeenth century, while the military sense is a collective use of the same noun.
intro.cn: force 经古法语来自晚期拉丁 fortia，这是由 fortis「强壮」构成的表「力量」的复数名词。物理义始于十七世纪，军事义则是同一名词的集体用法。

items.en: Fortis meant strong, mighty, able to resist; it described bodies, walls and men alike.
items.cn: fortis 意为强壮、有力量、能抵抗；它既能形容身体，也能形容城墙与人。

items.en: Late Latin fortia, a plural noun built on fortis, named strength or might; it is the form generally cited behind the French word.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 fortia 是由 fortis 构成的复数名词，指力量、威力；一般认为法语词就出自这个形式。

items.en: Old French force carried the noun into English in the thirteenth century with the senses of strength, violence and legal power.
items.cn: 古法语 force 在十三世纪把这个名词带入英语，带有力量、暴力与法律效力诸义。

items.en: By the medieval period force already covered armed bodies and the binding power of law, two branches that still run side by side.
items.cn: 到中世纪，force 已兼指武装队伍与法律的约束力，这两条分支至今并行。

items.en: Mechanics gave force its precise sense of a measurable push or pull, a use that became standard in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 力学赋予 force 可测量的推拉作用这一精确含义，这一用法在十七世纪成为标准。

items.en: The first dates for the physics sense and for the collective military sense are approximate; the noun itself is well attested from the medieval period.
items.cn: 物理义与集体军事义的最早记录年代为约数；这个名词本身在中世纪已有充分记录。

note.en: The first group either shares the Latin adjective for strong or merely looks like force; the second group separates force from neighbouring words for power and pressure.
note.cn: 第一组或共享那个表示「强壮」的拉丁形容词，或只是形似 force；第二组把 force 与相邻的「权力、压力」等词区分开。

entries.definition: From Latin fortis through French, but it names a stronghold, a place built to resist, not strength itself.
entries.definitionCN: 经法语来自拉丁 fortis，但指堡垒，即一座为抵抗而建的处所，不是力量本身。

entries.definition: From Italian forte 'strong', ultimately Latin fortis; it names a person's strong point, or a loud passage in music.
entries.definitionCN: 来自意大利语 forte「强壮」，最终出自拉丁 fortis；指一个人的长处，或音乐中响亮的段落。

entries.definition: A strengthened place, built on the same Latin adjective; it is a noun of place, not of power.
entries.definitionCN: 加固的城堡，由同一拉丁形容词构成；是表示地点的名词，不是力量。

entries.definition: From in- plus force: to put strength behind a rule so that it is obeyed.
entries.definitionCN: 由表「进入」的前缀加 force 构成：把力量放到规则背后，使其被遵守。

entries.definition: A smithy and the verb to shape metal; it comes from Latin fabrica 'workshop', not from fortis, so it only looks related.
entries.definitionCN: 指铁匠铺与锻打金属的动词；来自拉丁 fabrica「作坊」，而非 fortis，只是形似而已。

entries.definition: The quality of being strong in body or material; force can also mean the push itself.
entries.definitionCN: 身体或材料强健的性质；force 还能指推拉作用本身。

entries.definition: A broader word for ability or authority; force adds the idea of pressure applied.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指能力或权威的更宽说法；force 多一层「施加压力」的意思。

entries.definition: A steady push spread over a surface; force is the total push, pressure is that push divided by area.
entries.definitionCN: 分布在表面上的持续推力；force 是总推力，pressure 是单位面积上的推力。

entries.definition: Force used to injure or damage; it is the destructive edge of force.
entries.definitionCN: 用以伤害或破坏的力量；是 force 中带破坏性的那一面。

entries.definition: A verb for making someone act; force can do the same but also names the strength behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 使人行动的一个动词；force 也能这样用，但同时指背后的力量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Fortis is Latin for strong, and fortitude is the strength to endure.
normal.cn: fortis 是拉丁语「强壮」，fortitude 就是能坚持的力量。

normal.en: The family runs force, forced, forceful, enforce and reinforce.
normal.cn: 同族词有 force、forced、forceful、enforce 与 reinforce。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the main senses: come into force, labour force, air force, by force.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出主要义项：生效、劳动力、空军、强行地。

normal.en: Physics measures force in newtons, and every force has a direction.
normal.cn: 物理以牛顿为单位量力，每一个力都有方向。

normal.en: Law says a rule in force is one that can be enforced.
normal.cn: 法律说一条正在生效的规则，就是能被强制执行的那条。

abstract.en: Picture a bent beam slowly returning to a straight line under a jack.
abstract.cn: 想象一根弯梁在千斤顶下慢慢回到直线。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd leaning together against a gate until the hinges give way.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人一起压在门上，直到铰链撑不住。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing a stamp down hard enough to leave a mark.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手用力压下印章，留下清晰的痕迹。

examples.en: The engineers calculated the force needed to lift the span.
examples.cn: 工程师算出了抬起这跨梁所需的力。

examples.en: The old law is no longer in force.
examples.cn: 那条旧法律已不再生效。

examples.en: A strong wind forced the ferry to stay in port.
examples.cn: 大风迫使渡轮留在港内。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「for（为了）+ ce（策）」——为了推行一套策，就得使出力气；force 力量、武力、迫使

root: 拉丁 fortis「强壮」→ 晚期拉丁 fortia「力量」（复数）→ 古法语 force「力量、武力」→ 英语 force；物理「力」义自十七世纪力学，「部队」义由「兵力」的集体用法而来。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses grow from one strong hand: the hand pushes a body, shows its own strength, compels a person, backs a rule, moves a mind, gathers into a troop, is counted as manpower, and finally acts as a verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一只强壮的手长出：手推动物体、显出力气、强迫人、为规则撑腰、推动人心、聚成队伍、被计为人力，最后转为动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a strong hand that pushes until something yields.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只强壮的手一直推，直到某物让步。

branches.en: PUSH AND STRENGTH: a measurable push, and the plain strength a body or blow carries.
branches.cn: 推力与力气：可测量的推拉作用，以及身体或一击所带的直白力量。

branches.en: COMPULSION: the same push turned against a resisting person.
branches.cn: 强制：同一个推力转向一个抵抗的人。

branches.en: POWER BEHIND WORDS: a rule is enforced, an argument convinces, both by invisible pushing.
branches.cn: 言语背后的力量：规则被强制执行，论证说服人心，都是看不见的推力。

branches.en: STRENGTH IN NUMBERS: armed men and workers are gathered and counted as one force.
branches.cn: 人多成势：武装人员与工人被聚拢，计作一股力量。

branches.en: THE VERB: the hand that pushed becomes the act of forcing.
branches.cn: 动词：曾经推动的那只手，变成「迫使」这个动作。

intro.en: Force is a Latin noun of strength that became an English noun, verb and a whole family of derived words.
intro.cn: force 是一个表示力量的拉丁名词，在英语里成为名词、动词，并衍生出整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin fortis 'strong' gives fortia and force, and also fortitude, fort and fortress; the English prefix en- builds enforce from the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 fortis「强壮」衍生 fortia 与 force，也衍生 fortitude、fort 与 fortress；英语前缀 en- 由同一词干构成 enforce。

items.example: The adjective supplies the strength behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词为整个词族提供「力量」的底子。

items.structure: late Latin plural noun from fortis
items.example: The late Latin plural is the form usually cited behind the French noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个晚期拉丁复数，一般认为就是法语名词背后的形式。

items.example: The jack applied a steady force.

items.structure: force plus plural or third-person ending
items.example: Enemy forces withdrew from the valley.
She gave a forced smile and left.
items.exampleCN: 她勉强笑了一下就走开了。

items.example: The chair gave a forceful reply.
He argued forcefully for the repair fund.
items.exampleCN: 他为维修基金展开了有力的论证。

items.meaning: to put force behind a rule
items.meaningCN: 把力量加在规则上；执行
items.example: Officers enforce the parking ban every morning.
items.exampleCN: 执法人员每天上午执行禁停规定。

items.example: Steel bars reinforce the concrete wall.
items.exampleCN: 钢筋加固了这面混凝土墙。

definition_zh: 外国的；外来的；陌生的；无关的
definition_en: belonging to a country other than your own; coming from outside; strange and unfamiliar
core_image: 门外面、另一国土地上的东西
scene: 教室墙上贴着世界地图，老师指着远处的另一片大陆讲当地的风俗。She studies foreign languages at school.
sceneCN: 这里 foreign 是形容词「外国的」（第 1 个义项：属于别国的）；句意为她在学校学习外语。

derivatives.zh: 由 foreign 加名词后缀构成，义为「外国人；外乡人」
常用于指来自他国的人
由 foreign 加名词后缀构成，义为「异国性；陌生感」
由 foreign 加 born 构成，义为「出生在外国的」

senses.title: Belonging to another country
senses.definition: belonging to or connected with a country that is not yours
senses.definitionCN: 属于或关于他国的
senses.example: They import foreign cars.
senses.why: The core image is something standing beyond your own border.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是立于国境之外的东西。

senses.title: Coming from outside a place or body
senses.definition: entering a place or body from outside where it does not belong
senses.definitionCN: 从外部进入某个地方或身体、并不属于那里
senses.example: A foreign body in the eye hurts.
senses.why: The border is not only national; any boundary makes an inside and a foreign outside.
senses.whyCN: 边界不只在国与国之间，任何界线都会分出内与外。

senses.title: Strange and unfamiliar
senses.definition: strange, unfamiliar, or not belonging in a situation
senses.definitionCN: 奇怪、不熟悉或与处境格格不入
senses.example: Kindness was foreign to him.
senses.why: What lies outside your experience feels as far as another country.
senses.whyCN: 经验之外的东西，如同异国一样遥远。

intro.en: Foreign comes through French from Latin words about doors and thresholds.
intro.cn: foreign 经法语来自拉丁语中与门、门槛有关的词。

items.en: Latin foris meant outside, out of doors, beyond the threshold.
items.cn: 拉丁语 foris 意为在外、门外、门槛之外。

items.en: Medieval Latin foraneus meant lying outside, applied to towns beyond one's own.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 foraneus 意为处于外部，用于指自己属地之外的城镇。

items.en: Old French forain meant outside, especially outside the law or the community.
items.cn: 古法语 forain 意为外面的，尤指法律或共同体之外。

items.en: Middle English took forein or strange in law, commerce and travel.
items.cn: 中古英语吸收 forein，用于法律、商业与旅行语境。

items.en: Modern English fixed the national sense and added the metaphorical unfamiliar sense.
items.cn: 现代英语确立国家义项，并增加比喻性的陌生义。

note.en: Foreign has a tight family from the same Latin door.
note.cn: foreign 的词族都出自同一个拉丁「门」。

entries.definitionCN: 外国人；foreign 的派生词

entries.definition: lost as a penalty, outside the law
entries.definitionCN: 丧失的；罚金；同出 foris「门外」

海外的；在国外的

entries.definition: on or coming from the outside
entries.definitionCN: 外部的；外面的

normalIntro.en: Five anchors for the word foreign.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚定 foreign 记忆的方法。

normal.en: foreign hides for- (Latin foris, outside), like forfeit.
normal.cn: foreign 藏着 for-（拉丁语 foris「外面」），与 forfeit 同根。

normal.en: a foreigner is a person; foreign is the adjective.
normal.cn: foreigner 是人，foreign 是形容词。

normal.en: foreign language is the classroom word for a new tongue.
normal.cn: foreign language 是课堂里对一门新语言的称呼。

normal.en: foreign body in medicine means an intruding object.
normal.cn: 医学上 foreign body 指侵入体内的异物。

normal.en: foreign policy guides a country's dealings abroad.
normal.cn: foreign policy 指导一国的对外事务。

abstract.en: See a passport stamp from a far country.
abstract.cn: 想象来自远国的护照印章。

abstract.en: Feel the hush of stepping into an unknown street.
abstract.cn: 感受踏入陌生街道时的寂静。

abstract.en: See one red island floating outside the map border.
abstract.cn: 想象地图界外漂着一座红色孤岛。

examples.en: French is a foreign language for most of us.
examples.cn: 法语对我们多数人来说是外语。

examples.en: The doctor removed a foreign body from the wound.
examples.cn: 医生从伤口取出异物。

examples.en: Such cold weather is foreign to this island.
examples.cn: 这样的寒冷天气在这座岛上很罕见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗林」——拂开帘子看见外国：外国的

root: foreign 经古法语 forain 来自中世纪拉丁语 foraneus，追溯至拉丁语 foris「门外、外面」。一切「界外」之物皆可 foreign：别国的、体内的异物、经验之外的陌生事物。

sensesIntro.en: Foreign marks everything beyond a border: nations, bodies, and personal experience.
sensesIntro.cn: foreign 标记一切界外之物：国界、身体、以及个人经验之外。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: standing beyond the door, outside the line
core.cn: 核心意象：立于门外、越出界线

intro.en: Foreign shares its for- door with several family words; the list shows them.
intro.cn: foreign 与若干词共享 for- 这扇「门」，下面列出词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin foris means outside the door; from it come foreign, forfeit and forum, cousins by place and law.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 foris 意为门外，foreign、forfeit 与 forum 都出自它，以地点与法律相连。

items.exampleCN: 影片的异国情调打动了我们。
一位外国出生的市长发言。

items.meaning: to send a person across borders

definition_zh: 森林；林地；大量直立物形成的密集层
definition_en: a large area thickly covered with trees; the ecosystem formed by such an area; a dense mass of upright things
core_image: 一大片树冠彼此相接、从山脚一直铺到山脊的连续绿色
scene: 这片山地的森林从谷底一直铺到山脊，秋天一到，整面坡都变成金红色。 The forest on this mountainside runs from the valley floor up to the ridge, and in autumn the whole slope turns gold and red.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「覆盖山坡的大片森林」（第 1 个义项：大片树木覆盖的区域）；句意为这片山坡的森林从谷底延伸到山脊，秋天整面坡变成金红色。

pos.zh: 森林生态系统；森林生物群系
大量直立物形成的密集层
比喻义：只见细节不见整体（用于习语）

collocations.phrase: not see the forest for the trees

derivatives.zh: 有森林覆盖的
造林（少用）
林业；林地
林务员；森林居民
造林；使成为森林

senses.title: Large tree-covered area
senses.definition: a large area of land thickly covered with trees
senses.definitionCN: 大片被树木密集覆盖的土地
senses.example: The forest begins where the farmland ends.
senses.exampleCN: 森林从农田结束的地方开始。
senses.why: This is the everyday concrete sense: many trees over a large area.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常具体义：大片土地上的许多树。

senses.title: Forest ecosystem
senses.definition: the community of trees, plants, animals and soil processes that forms in such an area
senses.definitionCN: 在这样的区域形成的树木、植物、动物与土壤过程的整体
senses.example: The forest recycles most of its nutrients through leaf litter.
senses.exampleCN: 这片森林通过落叶回收大部分养分。
senses.why: Ecology treats the forest as a functioning system, not just a collection of trees.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把森林当作运作系统，而不只是树的集合。

senses.title: Dense upright mass
senses.definition: a large number of tall upright objects standing close together
senses.definitionCN: 大量高耸而直立的东西密集排列
senses.example: A forest of masts filled the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 港口里挤满了密集的桅杆。
senses.why: The tree image is transferred to any crowd of vertical objects.
senses.whyCN: 树的意象被转移到任何密集的直立物群。

senses.title: Royal hunting ground
senses.definition: a tract of land, often wooded, set aside by a king for hunting
senses.definitionCN: 国王划出用于狩猎的一片土地，常为林地
senses.example: The old forest law protected deer rather than farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 旧的王室林地法保护鹿，而不是农民。
senses.why: This is a legal and historical sense in which forest meant jurisdiction, not simply trees.
senses.whyCN: 这是法律与历史义：该词指管辖区域，而不只是树木。

senses.title: Whole versus detail
senses.definition: used in the idiom about failing to see the whole because of attention to small details
senses.definitionCN: 用于习语，指因专注细节而看不到整体
senses.example: The report missed the forest for the trees.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告只见树木不见森林。
senses.why: The word stands for the large pattern that detail can hide.
senses.whyCN: 这个词代表被细节遮住的大格局。

senses.title: Managed woodland
senses.definition: woodland managed as a resource for timber, fuel or conservation
senses.definitionCN: 作为木材、燃料或保护资源而经营的林地
senses.example: The forest is thinned every twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这片林地每二十年疏伐一次。
senses.why: The tree-covered area is treated as a crop with a rotation, so the forest becomes a managed resource.
senses.whyCN: 树木覆盖区被当作有轮伐期的作物，于是森林成为受管理的资源。

senses.title: Graph-theory forest
senses.definition: a graph with no cycles, equivalent to a set of disjoint trees
senses.definitionCN: 不含环的图，等价于一组互不相连的树
senses.example: A graph with no cycles is called a forest.
senses.exampleCN: 不含环的图被称为森林。
senses.why: Graph theory extends the tree image to a collection of trees.
senses.whyCN: 图论把树的意象扩展到一组树。

senses.title: Plant with trees (archaic)
senses.definition: to cover land with trees
senses.definitionCN: 在土地上种植树木
senses.example: Early settlers forested the valley slopes.
senses.exampleCN: 早期定居者在谷坡上植树成林。
senses.why: The verb is now rare and has been replaced by afforest and reforest.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词现在少见，已被「造林」与「重新造林」两个词取代。

intro.en: The legal and ecological senses both grow from a Medieval Latin term whose literal meaning is disputed but usually explained as 'outside wood'.
intro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 forestis 的字面义有争议，通常解释为「耕地之外的林地」；foris「外面」是较通行的来源，另一说未被普遍接受。

items.en: Medieval Latin forestis (silva) is first recorded in royal and legal documents. It probably meant woodland outside the cultivated area, though the exact sense is debated.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 forestis（silva）最早见于王室与法律文书。它可能指耕地之外的林地，但确切含义有争议。

items.en: The element is usually derived from foris 'outside, out of doors', related to forum. An alternative link to forestis 'of the forum' is disputed and not generally accepted.
items.cn: 该成分通常追溯到 foris「在外面、户外」，与 forum 有关。另一种把它联系到 forestis「广场的」的说法有争议，未被普遍接受。

items.en: Old French forest meant a large wood and also a royal hunting preserve. English borrowed it after the Norman Conquest.
items.cn: 古法语 forest 指大片树林，也指王室猎场。英语在诺曼征服后借入。

items.en: In English law a forest was a royal area with special hunting rights, which could include open land as well as trees.
items.cn: 在英国法律中，forest 是拥有特殊狩猎权的王室区域，可以包括树木，也可以包括开阔地。

items.en: With the rise of scientific forestry, forest shifted back toward its ecological meaning: a large tree-dominated community.
items.cn: 随着科学林业兴起，forest 又转向生态义：以树木为主的大片群落。

items.en: Twentieth-century ecology and mathematics added the ecosystem and graph-theory senses. The verb is now rare.
items.cn: 二十世纪的生态学与数学增加了生态系统义与图论义。动词用法现已少见。

note.en: The first group is close in sound or spelling but unrelated; the second group shares the tree-covered-area meaning at different scales.
note.cn: 第一组在读音或拼写上接近但无关；第二组在不同尺度上共享「树木覆盖区域」的意思。

entries.definition: a prediction, from fore- 'before' plus cast; it has no connection to forest.
entries.definitionCN: 预报。由 fore-「预先」加 cast 构成，与 forest 无关。

entries.definition: leading in position, from fore- plus most.
entries.definitionCN: 最前面的；首要的。由 fore- 加 most 构成。

entries.definition: a surname and given name meaning 'forest', spelled with a double r; it is a name, not the common noun.
entries.definitionCN: 福雷斯特。姓氏或名字，拼写为双 r，意为「森林」；是专名，不是普通名词。

entries.definition: a smaller area of trees than a forest; British usage often keeps wood for a modest patch.
entries.definitionCN: 树林。通常比 forest 小；英式用法常以 wood 指不大的一片。

entries.definition: land covered with trees, often used in ecology and land-use descriptions; it is less formal than forest and can be smaller.
entries.definitionCN: 林地。被树木覆盖的土地，常用于生态与土地利用描述；比 forest 少些正式感，面积也可更小。

entries.definition: a small group of trees, often of one kind or planted in a pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 小树林。一小群树，常为同一树种或有规则栽植。

entries.definition: dense tangled tropical vegetation; it stresses impenetrability, while forest is a neutral ecological term.
entries.definitionCN: 丛林。茂密纠缠的热带植被，强调难以穿行；forest 是中性生态术语。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The legal sense came first in English: a royal area with hunting rights, not necessarily all trees.
normal.cn: 英语中法律义先出现：拥有狩猎权的王室区域，不一定全是树。

normal.en: The ecological sense returned with scientific forestry in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.
normal.cn: 生态义随着十八、十九世纪的科学林业回归。

normal.en: Collocations: tropical forest, rain forest, forest floor, forest canopy.
normal.cn: 搭配：热带森林、雨林、林地地表、森林林冠。

normal.en: The idiom not see the forest for the trees means to miss the whole.
normal.cn: 习语「见树不见林」（not see the forest for the trees）意为只顾局部、看不到整体。

normal.en: Forestry, forester and afforest are the productive relatives.
normal.cn: forestry、forester 与 afforest 是能产的亲属词。

abstract.en: Picture a green sea that covers a whole valley and hides the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一片绿色的海覆盖整个山谷，把地面遮住。

abstract.en: Picture a harbour so full of masts that it looks like a vertical wood.
abstract.cn: 想象港口挤满桅杆，看上去像一片竖立的树林。

abstract.en: Picture a map where one large green patch is surrounded by small grey fields.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上一大块绿色被小块灰色农田包围。

examples.en: The forest on the ridge survived because the slope was too steep to log.
examples.cn: 山脊上的森林因为坡太陡无法采伐而保留下来。

examples.en: A forest of television towers rose above the stadium.
examples.cn: 一片电视塔像森林一样立在体育场上方。

examples.en: The old forest law allowed the king to hunt across private land.
examples.cn: 旧的王室林地法允许国王在私人土地上狩猎。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛瑞斯特」——一大片树连成绿色海洋 → 森林

root: 中世纪拉丁语 forestis（silva）最早见于王室法律文书，通常解释为「耕地之外的林地」，来源为拉丁语 foris「在外面」；另一说与 forestis「广场的」相关，未被普遍接受。后经古法语 forest 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a large tree-covered area to the ecosystem it forms, then to any dense upright mass, a legal hunting jurisdiction, a whole-versus-detail idiom, a managed resource, a graph without cycles and finally an archaic planting verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从大片树木覆盖区，到它形成的生态系统，再到任何密集直立物、法律狩猎辖区、整体与细节的习语、受管理资源、无环图，最后是古旧的植树动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a continuous green cover large enough to hide the ground beneath it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片足够大、能把地面遮住的连续绿色覆盖。

branches.en: AREA AND SYSTEM: the visible cover and the processes inside it.
branches.cn: 区域与系统：可见的覆盖与其内部的运作。

branches.en: VERTICAL TRANSFER: any dense upright mass becomes a forest.
branches.cn: 垂直转移：任何密集直立物都可成为森林。

branches.en: LAW AND MANAGEMENT: jurisdiction and resource are two ways of owning the cover.
branches.cn: 法律与经营：辖区与资源是拥有这片覆盖的两种方式。

branches.en: IDIOM: the large pattern that detail hides.
branches.cn: 习语：细节所遮蔽的大格局。

branches.en: ABSTRACT EXTENSIONS: graph theory and the archaic planting verb.
branches.cn: 抽象延伸：图论与古旧植树动词。

intro.en: Forest has a compact family built on a Medieval Latin base, with the legal and ecological senses layering over the same word.
intro.cn: forest 有一个建立在中世纪拉丁语基础上的紧凑词族，法律义与生态义层层叠在同一个词上。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin forestis and Latin foris supply the base, Old French forest transmits it, and English built forestry, forester and afforest.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 forestis 与拉丁语 foris 提供基础，古法语 forest 传递，英语构造了 forestry、forester 与 afforest。

latinEntries.structure: foresta, forestae (f., first declension, Medieval Latin)

items.example: The forest covers the whole valley.
Two forests meet at the river.
The upper slopes are heavily forested.

items.meaning: the act of planting with trees
items.example: Foresting the bare slope took decades.
items.exampleCN: 在裸坡上造林花了几十年。

items.meaning: the science or practice of managing forests
items.example: Forestry regulates how much timber is cut.

items.meaning: a person who manages or works in a forest
items.example: The forester marked the trees to be felled.
items.exampleCN: 林务员标记了要砍的树。

items.example: The scheme will afforest the eroded hillside.
items.exampleCN: 该计划将在受侵蚀的山坡造林。
毁林减少了集水区的覆盖。

items.meaning: a dense tropical forest with heavy rainfall
items.example: Rain forest canopy stays humid all year.
